title: Molecular Simulation and Expression Analysis of Vitamin C and Curcumin in Mitigating Buprofezin-induced Genotoxicity and Inflammatory Responses in Balb/c Mice.
authors: Sadia, Haleema; Qureshi, Irfan Zia; Naveed, Muhammad; Aziz, Tariq; Elkhadragy, Manal F; Alwethaynani, Maher S; Al-Asmari, Fahad; Alhhazmi, Areej A; Sagini, Hanan Abdulrahman; Almasoudi, Suad Hamdan; Al-Joufi, Fakhria A
one_liner_zh: 该文研究维生素C和姜黄素对杀虫剂诱导的小鼠基因毒性和炎症的保护作用，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白（NF-kB/TNF-alpha）而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且核心是毒理学与抗氧化机制，与本课题TF-DNA结合建模无关。
abstract: Buprofezin (BPFN), an extensively used insecticide, has raised concerns due to its potential genotoxic and pro-inflammatory effects in non-target organisms. This study aimed to assess the extent of BPFN-induced genotoxicity and inflammation in Balb/c mice and to evaluate the protective roles of two natural antioxidants, Vitamin C and curcumin (CUR). Male mice were orally administered BPFN at doses of 50, 100, and 250 mg/kg body weight for 28 days. Vitamin C and CUR (100 mg/kg each) were given individually or in combination. Genotoxicity was evaluated using the comet assay, which revealed significant DNA damage in both liver and kidney tissues, reflected by marked increases in comet length, head length, tail length, and olive tail moment (p < 0.001). Co-treatment with Vit C and CUR significantly reduced these genotoxic parameters (p < 0.001). Quantitative PCR analysis showed that BPFN exposure upregulated Interleukin-1beta (IL-1beta) mRNA expression by 4.28- to 7.94-fold in liver and 2.68- to 5.36-fold in kidney tissues (p < 0.001), while Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-alpha levels were also elevated and subsequently downregulated after antioxidant administration. Molecular docking analysis revealed that CUR had higher binding affinities with NF-kappaB (-9.8 kJ/mol) and TNF-alpha (-8.8 kJ/mol), whereas Vitamin C exhibited lower affinities (-6.2 kJ/mol for NF-kappaB and - 6.7 kJ/mol for TNF-alpha). Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that CUR maintained more stable interactions, with RMSD values ranging from 0.8 to 1.5 A, compared to Vitamin C (0.5 to 2.0 A). These findings highlight the protective efficacy of Vitamin C and curcumin-particularly in combination-against BPFN-induced genotoxic and inflammatory damage, suggesting their potential as mitigating agents in environmental toxicology contexts.
abstract_zh: Buprofezin (BPFN) 是一种广泛使用的杀虫剂，因其对非靶标生物具有潜在的遗传毒性和促炎作用而引发关注。本研究旨在评估BPFN诱导Balb/c小鼠遗传毒性和炎症的程度，并评价两种天然抗氧化剂维生素C和姜黄素 (curcumin, CUR) 的保护作用。雄性小鼠以50、100和250 mg/kg体重的剂量口服BPFN，持续28天。维生素C和CUR（各100 mg/kg）单独或联合给药。遗传毒性通过彗星实验 (comet assay) 评估，结果显示肝脏和肾脏组织中均出现显著DNA损伤，表现为彗星长度、头部长度、尾部长度和橄榄尾矩 (olive tail moment) 的显著增加 (p < 0.001)。维生素C和CUR联合处理显著降低了这些遗传毒性参数 (p < 0.001)。定量PCR分析显示，BPFN暴露使肝脏中白细胞介素-1β (Interleukin-1beta, IL-1beta) mRNA表达上调4.28至7.94倍，肾脏中上调2.68至5.36倍 (p < 0.001)，而白细胞介素-6 (Interleukin-6, IL-6) 和TNF-α水平也升高，并在抗氧化剂给药后下调。分子对接分析显示，CUR与NF-κB (-9.8 kJ/mol) 和TNF-α (-8.8 kJ/mol) 具有更高的结合亲和力，而维生素C表现出较低的亲和力（NF-κB为-6.2 kJ/mol，TNF-α为-6.7 kJ/mol）。分子动力学模拟表明，CUR维持了更稳定的相互作用，RMSD值范围为0.8至1.5 Å，而维生素C为0.5至2.0 Å。这些发现强调了维生素C和姜黄素——尤其是联合使用——对BPFN诱导的遗传毒性和炎症损伤的保护效力，提示它们作为环境毒理学背景下缓解剂的潜在应用价值。
